summary: Credit-transfer refill race causes short-window 429s for legacy API keys during high ingest
description:
Issue summary: Customer performed a credit transfer between two subaccounts and upgraded billing plan while running a large ingestion. After the transfer, several of their long-lived legacy API keys received intermittent 429 responses for ~18 minutes. Throttle headers were inconsistent across connections and some streaming sessions dropped mid-session.

Impact: Customer ingestion pipeline stalled; ~180k embedding tokens rejected with 429s, causing retries and duplicate downstream writes. Business impact: delayed nightly import and customer escalated to Enterprise CS.

Environment: Production (us-east), enterprise plan, legacy API keys issued in 2024, ingestion workload uses parallel uploader (16 workers) and keeps long-lived SSE streaming sessions open.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On enterprise org with two subaccounts A and B, initiate a credit transfer from A -> B via console transfer API.
2) Immediately after transfer, trigger a heavy parallel ingest from multiple hosts using legacy API keys tied to subaccount A.
3) Observe 429 responses and inconsistent X-RateLimit-* headers; streaming SSE sessions may drop with HTTP/2 CANCEL or 5xx from edge.
4) Note that console shows credits moved but quota refill windows did not align for some legacy keys.
investigation_notes: Support triage: customer provided X-RateLimit headers and ingestion timeline; initial hypothesis - delayed refill application for legacy key windows after credit transfer.
SRE checked quota-service metrics: observed brief backlog in refill-processor queue coinciding with transfer event; backlog caused per-key windows to be updated asynchronously and not atomically.
Edge/gateway logs show mixed window_reset values for requests from the same API key - indicates transient split-brain between token-windows cached at edge and authoritative quota-store.

Confirmed customer was using a mix of long-lived SSE connections and new short-lived upload connections; SSE sessions kept old local cache while new connections hit updated but not-yet-refilled windows, causing double-counting and short-window exhaustion.
Repro script created in staging to simulate transfer + concurrent workers; reproduced 429 spike when refill-processor latency > 8s and when edge cache TTL > 10s.

Related code area: quota-service async refill path + edge cache invalidation. Investigated PR history and found a recent change that optimized bulk credit writes but did not force immediate cache invalidation for legacy-key windows (PR referenced above).
Dashboard links: RateLimiter queue depth: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ratelimiter/refill-queue?orgId=1 (observed spike at 03:12)
Customer impact estimate: ~180k tokens rejected, ingestion throughput reduced by 70% during spike window.
comments: Aisha Kumar (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported 429s started immediately after credit transfer. Provided request IDs and sample headers.
Evelyn Park (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging; noticed refill-processor backlog. Opening an engineering investigation and escalating to infra-oncall. Linked PR for quick fix.

Tomás Rivera (Infra Eng) 2026-03-11: Deployed a hotfix to force synchronous cache invalidation for credit-transfer flow (edge cache TTL bypass for affected keys). Monitoring for 60 minutes post-deploy.
Customer (NimbusSearch) 2026-03-11: Confirmed ingest resumed and 429s subsided; saw backlog clear and normal throughput restored. Asked for root-cause and permanent fix ETA.
Evelyn Park (SRE) 2026-03-12: Follow-up - engineering merged PR 5487 which adds atomic refill + cache invalidation and adds a guard to avoid refill backlogs. Will monitor during next billing cycles.
root_cause: Race between async credit-transfer refill path and edge cache TTL for legacy API keys. Bulk credit write optimized path did not trigger immediate cache invalidation, causing mismatched token-window state and transient 429s under concurrent connections.
resolution: Hotfix applied: synchronous cache invalidation for credit-transfer flow and immediate refill queue prioritization for affected subaccounts. Engineering merged permanent fix (PR 5487) to make refill + cache update atomic. Manual quota-sync executed for the customer's affected keys to restore normal windows. Customer ingestion completed without further 429s.
resolution_notes: Hotfix timeline: 03-10 03:25 UTC - applied edge cache bypass for the specific org; 03-10 04:00 UTC - manual quota-sync completed; 03-11 09:12 UTC - PR 5487 deployed to prod.

Postmortem actions: add unit/integration tests to simulate credit-transfer + concurrent sessions, add alert on refill-processor queue depth, and add docs for customers about safe timing window after billing changes.
Follow-up task: INT-3025 to add a console notice when credit-transfer in progress and recommended best practices for high-throughput ingests.
follow_up_tasks: Write KB article: Safe windows after billing and credit transfers
public_response: We investigated and found a transient race during your credit transfer that briefly left some legacy API key limits out-of-sync with the authoritative quota store. We applied a fix and manually resynced affected keys; this should prevent recurrence. We recommend pausing large ingests for 60 seconds after transfers or upgrades until the console confirms credits are active.
notes_for_engineering: Add atomic refill+invalidation for all bulk credit paths. Consider opt-in immediate-consistency mode for enterprise orgs performing large transfers. Verify staging tests cover long-lived SSE + concurrent worker scenarios.
